subject: microbiology
title: Metachromatic Granules and Tellurite Medium in Diphtheria Diagnosis

steps.tx: **Metachromatic granules** are polyphosphate energy stores (volutin, Babes Ernst bodies) packed at Corynebacterium poles, staining reddish purple with toluidine blue and bluish black in Albert stain because the dye changes colour on the polymer (metachromasia). Richest on Loeffler serum medium, scarce on ordinary agar, they are a culture medium effect examiners love.
steps.say: Granules are phosphate batteries that change dye colour; serum medium fattens them for the stain.

right.title: Granule display
points: Neisser: granules brown black, bodies yellow

steps.tx: **Potassium tellurite medium** selects corynebacteria by tellurite tolerance and reads reduction to black metallic tellurium (grey black colonies), suppressing throat commensals, with biotype traditions (mitis smooth, gravis daisy head rough, intermedius small) once guiding epidemiology. Cystine tellurite blood agar is its modern blood enriched form.
steps.say: Tellurite blackens diphtheria colonies while silencing the throat crowd.

left.title: Tellurite design
points: Colonies grey black in 24 to 48 hours

steps.tx: **Biotypes gravis, mitis and intermedius** divided diphtheria by colony, haemolysis and fermentation (gravis starch and glycogen fermenter, severe reputation), now replaced by ribotyping and genome sequencing for outbreaks, belfanti split taxonomically. Historical severity associations were strain toxin and setting, not biotype destiny.
steps.say: Gravis sounded graver; genome typing replaced colony morphology for outbreak truth.

left.title: Biotype heritage
points: Gravis: rough daisy head, starch positive
Belfanti: nitrate negative separate species now

right.title: Modern typing
points: Whole genome clusters and tox alleles
Biotype retained in examinations, not reports

steps.tx: **Specimen pathway for suspected diphtheria** swabs beneath the membrane edge and throat plus nose, plated to blood, Loeffler and tellurite, alerting the laboratory by telephone because routine throat benches discard coryneforms, with toxin PCR at reference laboratories same day where systems allow.
steps.say: Swab under the membrane and telephone the bench, or diphtheroids get discarded as flora.

nodes.label: Swabs from membrane edge, nose and throat
Reference tox PCR and Elek confirmation

steps.tx: **Iron and toxin regulation** (DtxR repressor binding tox promoter when iron plentiful) explains why diphtheria toxin pours under iron starvation in the throat and why laboratory toxin production needs low iron media (Elek conditions). Low iron in tissue is the signal the phage gene evolved to obey.
steps.say: Iron plenty, toxin off; iron scarce, toxin on: DtxR is diphtheria's thermostat.

left.title: Regulation mechanics
points: Host nutritional immunity starves iron (calprotectin kin)

right.title: Bench consequences
points: Toxin yield varies by strain and medium
PCR detects gene, Elek detects expression
Non toxigenic tox bearing strains (expression broken) exist

steps.tx: **Non toxigenic diphtheriae** still cause invasive disease (endocarditis, bacteraemia, especially in disadvantaged and injecting populations) and throat carriage, and can acquire phage in situ theoretically, so species identification in sterile sites matters even where Elek is negative. Toxin negativity closes one question, not the isolate's file.
steps.say: No toxin does not mean no disease: non toxigenic strains still invade valves.

left.title: Non toxigenic disease
points: Outbreaks in homeless and injecting networks

steps.tx: **Differential morphology** sorts throat bacilli: Klebsiella Loeffler bacillus heritage name for diphtheriae itself, diphtheroids shorter and granule poor, streptococci cocci obviously, Vincent fusospirochaetes in ulcerative tonsillitis, and Candida pseudomembranes that wipe off (diphtheria membrane bleeds). Bedside membrane behaviour precedes microscopy.
steps.say: Candida wipes, diphtheria bleeds: membrane behaviour is the first differential test.

right.title: Diphtheria clues
points: Extends beyond tonsil to uvula and palate
Bull neck and serosanguineous nasal discharge

steps.tx: **Albert stain viva pairing** closes: best medium Loeffler, best stain Albert (or Neisser), granule chemistry polyphosphate, tellurite black, toxigenicity Elek, immunity Schick (next lessons). Each named answer guards one variable, as sterilisation tests did, examiners rotate them in sequence. A question may jump between these pegs without warning, which is why the sequence is rehearsed as one chain.
steps.say: Medium, stain, granule, tellurite, tox, immunity: diphtheria answers rotate on six named pegs.

right.title: Beyond bench
points: Antitoxin: therapy cannot wait any of these
